title.en: Wildlife and biosphere reserves of India

text.en: India shelters about 81,251 species of animals, from the Asian elephant to the Bengal tiger. Many are in danger, so the nation protects them.

Wildlife includes all non-domesticated animals, both vertebrates and invertebrates.
India has about 81,251 animal species, out of about 1.5 million in the world.
Hunting, poaching and loss of habitat have driven some species to extinction.
The Indian Board for Wildlife was set up in 1952 and the Wildlife (Protection) Act was passed in 1972.
India has 106 National Parks and about 573 Wildlife Sanctuaries.
Project Tiger was launched in April 1973 to conserve tigers in Tiger Reserves.
Biosphere reserves protect large areas of natural habitat with buffer zones open to some economic use; India has 18 of them.
Eleven of them, including the Nilgiris, Gulf of Mannar, Agasthiyamalai, Nanda Devi, Sundarbans and Great Nicobar, are in UNESCO's Man and Biosphere programme.

problem.en: How do biosphere reserves differ from national parks?

text.en: A national park is strictly reserved for wildlife.
A biosphere reserve has a core, plus a buffer zone open to some economic uses.

why.en: People are part of the system.

text.en: So biosphere reserves balance protection with livelihood.
